correctness.rationale: The sorted-direction Minkowski vertex formula gives a_i=sum_j binomial(i-1,j-1), with strict ordering. Subset cuts give precisely C_{n,k}(s), and the difference body has every subset normal as a facet. An origin-centered insphere and strict tangency prove no other narrowest normals. At k=n the count factorizes. Exactly 36 finite strict squared comparisons cover n=3..14, and for n>=15 a monotonic derivative of h(t), separate s=2,3,4 bounds, and a global singleton-versus-balanced comparison prove the sharp switch. The finite checker independently verifies all 36 base inequalities, 3599 profile comparisons through n=120, 139 cut formulas and 14 exact vertex constructions; none replaces the infinite tail proof.

value.rationale: The object is the canonical all-tube simplex-sum graph-associahedron of complete graphs, a standard geometric realization, and its Euclidean minimum thickness is a meaningful intrinsic metric invariant. A sharp singleton-to-balanced transition at exactly 15 vertices, complete equality classification and axis multiplicities provide a structural statement in all dimensions, not merely a reformulation or one small finite computation. The exact formula for every intermediate member is a useful, but secondary, computable invariant. The prior biclique and fixed-rank results do not make the all-subsets exact phase an automatic corollary.
